how: A member proposes a trans flag and another opening gathers offers, practical building advice and coordinates.
Calls recruit flag builders and later extend participation to defense, ace text and an agender heart.
Members answer defense calls with brief reports of participation or offers to help.
A participant rejects an oversized flag because available hands and occupied artwork make its scale impractical.
An objection about insufficient hands and harm to existing art ends an oversized proposal before construction rather than triggering relocation.
Workers negotiate flag color, orientation, extent and additions rather than adopting a wholly new emblem.
Promoting a visible mark need not mean advertising its support room when members fear hostile visitors.
Members report building, progress pictures, locations and the flag's changing state.
Coordinates and color corrections guide workers without demonstrating a pixel-by-pixel design template.
Members use spare accounts to maintain marks and later credit hundreds of placements across their alts.
A single room cannot test the cross-room prevalence claim, and its reported sticky rule prevents treating distributed work as absence of decided norms.
Builders prioritize maintenance, coordinate repairs and defend flags, hearts and text against changing pixels.
Members attribute damage, dispute enemy motives and correct mistaken classifications of placers and marks.
A threatened mark is reclassified as friendly when its maker reports helping defend the sign and another member backs preservation.
Members assert non-harm norms, route around artwork, refuse punitive escalation and apologize with offers to restore damage.
Restraint is negotiated and breached rather than universal, as a member celebrates overwriting Mario while others request preservation.
Participants report neighbor contact, discuss crossing routes and relay an artwork agreement from the dedicated flag venue.
A member reports contact with neighboring builders while another brings an overlapping artwork request into the thread.
Neighboring participants offer defense, receive welcomes and thank builders for preserving both works.
Recruiting across kindred subs and linking a dedicated flag venue do not establish a coalition agreement or shared governance.
Requests to weave or add a neighboring heart do not establish a host ruling over guest works.
The record shows an abandoned oversized proposal and rebuilding the road but does not document moving after losing a held spot.
Reported rules and restoration promises do not show members disputing who can commit the group to an agreement.
Participants bring trans identity and visibility into flag work and interpret its survival through everyday struggles and belonging.
Retrospective political discussion celebrates the failed Trump image and disputes a conspiracy account.
Political side discussion also repairs factual comparisons through a sourced correction and explicit acceptance.
Naming hostile groups or celebrating their failure does not establish a quarrel carried into the canvas from an earlier exchange.
Enemy attributions and retrospective political satisfaction do not link a prior tie to the room's own attack in the same turn.
Workers use a dedicated flag subreddit and relay its instructions while retaining discussion in the support room.
Members dispute whether defending pixels matters without settling where canvas posts may appear.
An injury exchange explicitly keys one impossible hormone answer as April Fools while other replies give reassurance and practical advice.
Joking is locally marked within an ordinary care exchange and does not establish that flag mobilization was a prank.
Participants celebrate visibility, thank defenders and make small contributions meaningful as collective belonging.
A visible stripe becomes recognizable as the community's flag only after a viewer asks for directions and receives an explanation.
Members mark the end, display the result and recall how the spanning stripe endured.
One participant wishes the completed work would become a poster without demonstrating an organized continuation.
A retrospective reply corrects the implied responsibility for neighboring damage by citing repeated non-harm instructions and a sticky rule.
A member reports overwriting Mario while other exchanges propose paving over a strip or removing an arrow.
Members celebrate hostile imagery's failure after the event without showing that they conducted the attacks.
The building call receives an offer to contribute and practical flag-building instructions.
The proposal already functions as a call, and the next opening does not establish that one starter caused a separate recruitment stage.
A participant explicitly explains that completed flag work remains vulnerable to changed pixels and therefore requires protection.
Neighbor restraint and route negotiation also arise while expanding, so upkeep pressure cannot explain all border talk.
Non-harm instructions precede reported neighbor contact, so a settled bargain is not necessary for restraint.
Alt accounts are reported during upkeep, but the record does not establish adoption because single-account placements proved insufficient.
Participants explicitly celebrate the built stripe and thank everyone who worked on it.
Progress images, celebration and final display coexist without demonstrating that celebration caused preservation.
The poster wish is visible but is not shown to result from recording the work.
The insufficient-hands exchange concerns starting an oversized addition rather than abandoning a held spot, and ends without a move.
Design corrections and coordinates occur without a documented template settling the design pixel by pixel.
The defense call receives brief acceptances, while disagreement about defense is answered with reasons.
An outsider explicitly cites the flag's ongoing struggle while reporting an hour of help and receives a welcome.
Reported contact, thanks and assistance do not establish an exchange of space for upkeep.
Recruitment and destructive proposals are both visible, but the record does not show that recruitment turned builders toward attacking rivals.
An arrow-removal proposal receives the maker's reasoned preservation request and another member's support for keeping it.
The arrow-removal proposal leads to identification and preservation rather than a documented truce negotiation.
Retrospective satisfaction at rivals' losses does not establish a sequence from this room's own attack call to contest talk.
Defense and cross-room help are documented but do not demonstrate joining a coalition under strain.
Dedicated coordination and concern about hostile exposure are visible without evidence that a flood of recruitment posts caused the venue boundary.
Agreement reminders and retrospective denials of responsibility do not show an authority dispute following a deal.
